the problem of predicting the emergence of new concepts in social streams.
the problem of identifying nascent entities in the setting of real-time social streams, where the goal is to identify entities that will be relevant for the knowledge base in the near future.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is a promising step towards automatic generation of pseudo-ground truth in the setting of entity linking and knowledge base construction.
our method is effective in generating pseudo-ground truth in a setting where the ground truth is missing.
our method is a significant step forward in the task of predicting new concepts in social streams.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are able to identify new emerging entities with a high precision and recall, by using a pseudo-ground truth generation method that is able to deal well with missing labels, and that leverages entity confidence scores and document quality.
we present a new method to generate pseudo-ground truth for predicting new concepts in social streams, which can be used to train a named entity recognizer that can be used in real time applications.
, we present a method for generating pseudo ground truth for training an entity recognizer in a fast paced domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pseudo-ground truth generation is feasible in the context of social streams and that it can be used to improve the identification of nascent concepts in real-world settings.
it is possible to leverage pseudo-ground truth to identify nascent concepts and improve the quality of entity linking in social streams.
it is possible to train an entity recognition system to identify nascent entities in real-time applications, and to do so in a way that is robust to missing labels.
